instruction:
We act for Bredeix Organic Creamery, LLC, an organic dairy processor that also runs milk procurement, which is licensing software from Laipeisk Systems, Inc. Before Bredeix commits, the client wants to know what in this package exposes it to risk and what we should push back on.

Please review all four documents in the matter folder: the software license agreement (bredeix_laipeisk_software_license_agreement.md), the Phase 2 statement of work (statement_of_work_phase2.md), the data processing addendum (data_processing_addendum.md), and the insurance certificate cover letter (insurance_certificate_cover_letter.md).

Send me a memo that lists each issue you find. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters to Bredeix in light of how the client operates, and recommend a fix. Where you can, put the fix in proposed language. Order the issues by how much they matter to the client, and flag anything you think needs a call with the client before we respond to Laipeisk.

rubric.text: The response concludes that the Data Processing Addendum's liability clause brings Personal Data Breach liability back under the liability cap (about 12 months' fees), overriding the License Agreement's Section 11.3(c) carve-out that left data-security breaches uncapped.
The response identifies the data-breach cap issue as located in the Data Processing Addendum, Section 8.1.
For the DPA data-breach cap issue, the response explains why it matters to Bredeix and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the pending sale of Bredeix's parent (to Northfold Provisions Group) is an indirect Change of Control under the License Agreement that requires Laipeisk's prior written consent, which has not been given.
The response identifies the change-of-control issue as arising under License Agreement Section 16.2.
For the change-of-control issue, the response explains why it matters to Bredeix and recommends a fix.
The response concludes that Bredeix's August 7, 2026 Phase 1 Rejection Notice was untimely because the 10-day rejection window running from the July 20, 2026 Delivery had already closed.
The response identifies the late-rejection issue as located in the Statement of Work Section 2.2 or License Agreement Section 6.2.
For the late Phase 1 rejection issue, the response explains why it matters to Bredeix and recommends a fix.
The response concludes that the License Agreement renews automatically for five-year terms unless non-renewal notice is given within a narrow window of 120 to 90 days before the end of the term.
The response identifies the auto-renewal issue as located in License Agreement Section 14.2.
For the auto-renewal issue, the response explains why it matters to Bredeix and recommends a fix.
The response states that under the License Agreement's order-of-precedence clause the DPA prevails over the License Agreement as to Personal Data.
The response is a memo that presents the issues in an order ranked by their importance to the client.
The response flags at least one point that it says should be discussed with the client before responding to Laipeisk.
The response claims that Bredeix's August 7, 2026 Rejection Notice was timely under the acceptance provisions.
The response claims that data-breach liability remains uncapped under the License Agreement's Section 11.3(c) notwithstanding the DPA.
